correctness.rationale: The opposite-sign parabola-chord criterion is necessary and sufficient for an interior target moment. Disjoint outer-spread and inner-hole events yield two exact one-dimensional integrals and an independent two-variable success integral. The inner exponent has a unique nondegenerate interior maximum with curvature -2/(pi sqrt(q(1-q))); the outer exponent has two equal endpoint maxima, contributing exactly 2r_out^m. Their strictly monotone rates cross uniquely at q=1/3. Direct finite quadrature and 1,200 independent linear-program comparisons support, but do not replace, this full analytic argument. Checks in verify.py passed on the extracted final file.

value.rationale: This is a natural sample-design choice for positive numerical quadrature of a uniform target, not an arbitrarily selected invariant: the Chebyshev distribution clusters samples near endpoints, changing the competition between central-hole and spread obstructions. The exact 1/3 crossover, sharp sqrt(m) prefactor, and provable exponential improvement over uniform-node sampling offer a precise criterion for selecting node count at prescribed feasibility confidence. The statement does not need a general algorithm or higher-degree extension to be valuable; it deliberately does not assert weight conditioning.
